source.title: Broken Neural Scaling Laws
source.authors: Ethan Caballero; Kshitij Gupta; I. Rish; D. Krueger

record.tranche_reason: The paper mentions grokking and reports its own scaling experiments on 4-digit addition, but it does not test the delayed train-versus-test generalization behavior or any other listed claim version.
record.gate_note: The paper cites grokking as an example of an arithmetic task with a sharp scaling inflection. Its own arithmetic results concern test performance versus training dataset size and training steps; the text does not report training accuracy, overfitting, a delay after training accuracy saturates, or how that delay changes with dataset size. No result directly tests a listed version.
record.test_reason: The paper fits a broken power law to scaling curves. It mentions grokking only as an example of an inflection point in scaling behaviour. Its own 4-digit addition experiments plot test performance against dataset size and training steps, with no training-accuracy curve and no measure of a delay after overfitting. No result bears on any version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is essentially correct. The authors conclude that BNSL models and extrapolates diverse scaling behaviours, including double descent and the sharp inflection in 4-digit addition, better than prior functional forms. They also conclude that sharp breaks limit predictability: points near or after the break are needed to extrapolate.
record.recipe_differences: The paper fits a broken-power-law scaling form to performance curves; it does not reproduce the grokking training procedure or measure the train/test trajectory described in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: For 4-digit addition, accurate extrapolation depends on including training-dataset-size points near the break: the authors report that points from at least dataset size 720 are needed with noisy runs, and at least 415 in a noiseless simulation; the break is around size 415.

fits_no_version.finding: 4-digit addition performance shows a sharp inflection as training dataset size varies, with the break around 415 examples. BNSL extrapolates the curve only when fitted points reach at least size 720 (at least 415 in a noiseless simulation).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sharp breaks in arithmetic-task scaling curves limit how early they can be extrapolated by curve fitting.

record.problems: The arithmetic results relevant to the claim are presented in figures, without textual values for the curve. The paper does not report training accuracy alongside test performance, so its arithmetic scaling results cannot establish the claimed overfitting-to-generalization delay.

untested.parts: No training accuracy is reported, so neither the delay after training saturation nor its dependence on dataset size can be read.
No delayed generalization measured on non-algorithmic data, and no manipulation of initialization scale or weight norm.
No measurement of delayed generalization in LLM pretraining or fine-tuning.
Weight decay is fixed at 0.1 and not varied. No ungrokking test.
Algorithms learned across runs are not compared.
Optimizer and numerical choices are not varied.

record.verdict_notes: The relation is changed from 'discusses' to 'cites_only'. Grokking (Power et al.) appears only in one introductory sentence as an example of an inflection point. The 4-digit addition setup (Adam optimizer, weight decay 0.1, full-batch training) resembles grokking setups, but no train/test gap is reported.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not report training accuracy or overfitting, a delayed test-accuracy rise after training accuracy saturates, or how optimization delay changes as the training set shrinks.
No circuit formation, memorizing-component removal, or continuous mechanism measure is reported.
No test of grokking-like delays across non-algorithmic data or of initialization scale, weight norm, or a lazy-to-rich transition.
No test of delayed generalization in realistic large-model pretraining or fine-tuning.
No test of a low-norm efficiency account, critical dataset size, or ungrokking.
No comparison of whether runs converge to the same identifiable algorithm.
No test of optimizer or numerical artifacts as an explanation for grokking.

rows.subject: transformer model (4-digit addition task)
rows.operation_detail: Varied training dataset size for the 4-digit addition task.

conditions.value: Each point is the mean of greater than 1000 seeds.

rows.measure: 4-digit addition scaling behavior; the measure is not stated in the text accompanying the figure.
rows.locator: Figure 5 left; Sections 5.5 and A.5; Table 5
rows.note: The authors state that the curve has an inflection point and that BNSL models and extrapolates it. The text does not report a train/test accuracy gap or grokking delay.
rows.check: Performance across dataset sizes (144-1008) at the end of training is a scaling curve, not a train/test trajectory. The y-axis metric is not stated in the text. The row reports a BNSL fit of the study's own method, not a grokking measurement.

rows.subject: transformer model (4-digit addition task)
rows.operation_detail: Varied number of training steps and measured test cross-entropy.

conditions.value: Each point is the mean of greater than 600 seeds.

rows.note: The authors state that BNSL accurately extrapolates the scaling behavior. They do not state that test performance rises long after training accuracy saturates.
rows.check: Test cross-entropy versus training steps at dataset size 992, with no training accuracy or loss reported. A delay after training saturation cannot be read. The value is shown only in a figure, and the row serves to demonstrate the study's own fitting method.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
